meta.title: Japanese — Idioms and Proverbs
meta.subtitle: 206 four-character idioms and proverbs — after the levels
meta.desc: Japanese idioms: four-character compounds (yojijukugo, 一石二鳥 "killing two birds with one stone") and proverbs — the counterpart of the Mandarin deck's chengyu. 206 idioms, each ONE note with TWO cards. THE SELECTION: every entry JMdict tags as a four-character idiom or a proverb, not already in the JLPT decks, that the Tatoeba corpus uses in at least 2 sentences, commonest first — of the 2,780 the dictionary tags, most of which a learner never meets. Idiomatic phrases with a literal twin (花が咲く, 頭が痛い) are left out: the corpus's sentences for them are nearly all literal, so they would teach the idiom over the wrong sentence. Each card carries furigana, Hepburn romaji, the meanings, a row per kanji, and real sentences. — Phrases, readings and meanings: JMdict (Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, CC BY-SA 4.0). Furigana: JmdictFurigana (CC BY-SA 4.0). Kanji: KANJIDIC2 (EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0) and KanjiVG (CC BY-SA 3.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR; the readings over them come from segmenting the corpus with MeCab and UniDic, so a reading over an example sentence is a machine's and can occasionally be wrong — the headword's own reading is the dictionary's.
